ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, proposed managers, and authorized signatories against: (i) French DG Trésor asset-freeze decisions; (ii) EU consolidated autonomous sanctions lists; (iii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iv) OFAC SDN List where transactions involve USD or United States financial counterparties; and (v) FATF high-risk jurisdiction alerts. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are subject to enhanced due diligence, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification. Screening is ongoing, event-driven on list updates, documented, and retained in accordance with Article L.561-8 and Article R.561-20 of the Code monétaire et financier.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); RCS consultation and pre-clearance verification through Infogreffe (infogreffe.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate filings and the proposed name must be in the Latin alphabet and rendered in French. A non-French-language corporate name must be transliterated into Latin characters and must be usable in French; the legal form suffix "SARL" is mandatory. Accented characters are permissible, but the name must be sufficiently distinctive from all existing RCS entries and protected trademarks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may: (1) file a written request for reconsideration through the INPI Guichet Unique within 15 days of the registrar's notice; (2) if the refusal is based on a conflicting prior right, submit a deed of consent from the earlier right-holder or a commercial-court order; (3) where the registrar maintains the refusal, bring a summary or merits application before the competent Tribunal de commerce under Code de commerce Article L.123-5; and (4) in the alternative, file a new distinctive name, which restarts the 30-day name-clearance window. No statutory extension of the existing reservation is available.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or serviced office is permissible for RCS registration only if it corresponds to a real, identifiable French address capable of receiving official mail and service of process. Pure letterbox arrangements without local management, books, accounts, and bank accounts in France are disallowed and may be disregarded by the tax administration under Article 209 B CGI and the abuse-of-law procedure in Article L.64 of the Livre des procédures fiscales. For an aircraft-engine dry-leasing SARL, the registered office should be supported by substantive management presence in France.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified at approximately 25% unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months for a standard SARL, increasing to 45% when cross-border leasing invoices and VAT refunds are involved. DGFiP may conduct on-site inspections without prior notice under Article L.16 B of the Livre des procédures fiscales, and URSSAF may also control social-security registration at the registered office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), attached to the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté Industrielle et Numérique; taxpayer portal: impots.gouv.fr; corporate registration portal: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique); the dedicated non-resident corporate filing office is the Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE), 10 rue du Centre, 93465 Noisy-le-Grand Cedex; customs (export/EORI) authority: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: incorporate the SARL via the Guichet Unique portal with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce to obtain the INSEE-issued SIREN (9 digits), SIRET (14 digits) and the APE/NAF code (ISIC 5223 maps to French NAF 52.23Z, services auxiliaires des transports aériens). A classic SARL has no minimum capital requirement; non-resident shareholders are permitted. Step 2: within 15 days of legal incorporation, file the statement of existence and constitutional documents (liasse fiscale) with the territorial SIE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) to open the corporate tax file and obtain the internal tax account number. Step 3: obtain VAT registration: the established French SARL files Cerfa form 14463*01 with the SIE (or with the SIEE when the company is foreign-controlled) to receive the intra-Community VAT identification number (FR + 11 characters) and, issued by DGDDI, the EORI number (FR + SIREN) used for customs declarations. Step 4: open a French bank account and document the banking domiciliation required under the exchange-control regime. Step 5: file recurring returns: yearly corporate income tax (Cerfa 2065-SD with annexes 2050-2065) and VAT return (Cerfa 3310-CA3) under the real regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope (the French-resident SARL is a capital company taxed as a separate taxpayer on profits of enterprises operated in France under Article 209-I CGI; profits attributable to foreign branches are de facto exempt under the French territoriality principle, with recapture of losses; the SARL is not a pass-through entity and is not situated in a tax-exempt zone).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available elections: (1) SARL de famille option for partnership-like transparency under Article 239 bis AA CGI, restricted to close-family shareholders, making the SARL transparent for income tax purposes; (2) French fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI, elected by a French parent holding at least 95% of subsidiaries, consolidating group taxable results for periods of five years; (3) option to waive the franchise en base de TVA threshold and enter the normal VAT regime under Article 293 F CGI; (4) option to form a VAT group (assujetti unique) under Article 256 C bis CGI for entities with financial, economic and organisational links; (5) OSS/IOSS elections for intra-EU distance sales and digital services through the single French VAT portal, and (6) the Article 137 option already exercised by France which grants the right to deduct input VAT on the Article 262-II-1° aircraft-international exemption. France does not operate a check-the-box system; hybrid mismatch outcomes are corrected unilaterally under the ATAD 2 provisions (Articles 212 bis and 223 quinquies CGI) through double-deduction, deduction/non-inclusion, branch and hybrid-transfer adjustment mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA) - Articles 256 to 289 ter of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI), implementing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; administered by DGFiP.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: The domestic small-business VAT exemption (franchise en base) under Article 293 B CGI applies to a French-established SARL: for sales of goods, EUR 91,900 basic threshold and EUR 101,000 closing threshold; for supplies of services (including dry leasing of aircraft engines, treated as a supply of services), EUR 36,800 basic threshold and EUR 40,800 closing threshold (Loi de finances 2023 values). The franchise does not shield non-established foreign suppliers, nor does it apply when the taxpayer opts to be taxed. For intra-EU distance sales and telecommunications/broadcasting/e-services, a EUR 10,000 per-calendar-year OSS threshold applies. Because the SARL is French-established, it must register for VAT regardless of turnover whenever it performs taxable activities requiring a VAT number to claim zero rating or input VAT deduction, or once turnover exceeds the franchise thresholds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured electronic invoicing (facturation électronique) for domestic B2B transactions, introduced by Loi de Finances 2020 (Article 153) and Décret n° 2022-1299 of 7 October 2022. From 1 September 2026 all taxpayers must be able to receive e-invoices and large and mid-size companies must issue them; from 1 September 2027 all companies, including small and micro entities, must issue e-invoices. Invoices must use structured formats (Factur-X, UBL 2.1 or CII, conforming to EN 16931) and be transmitted through a certified Partner Dematerialisation Platform (PDP) or the public Portail Public de Facturation (PPF). France applies a 'Y'-type model: no pre-clearance or fiscal stamping by the tax authority, but continuous e-reporting (transaction and payment data) to DGFiP. Authentication and integrity are assured by qualified electronic signature or seal. Exports outside the EU remain governed by the DGDDI digital customs environment (DELTA-G / DES-D2023 and the DUA), and intra-EU dispatches require Intrastat/DEB filings when value thresholds are met.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: (1) Exports outside the EU are exempt at 0% with the right to deduct input VAT under Article 262-I-1° CGI when the goods (an aircraft engine sold or permanently removed) physically leave EU territory, evidenced by customs and transport documentation; (2) under Article 262-II-1° CGI, the supply, hire and dry leasing of aircraft engines incorporated into aircraft used by airlines performing predominantly international operations is exempt; France has exercised the Article 137 option so this exemption confers the right to deduct input VAT, provided the lessor can prove the airline's international-route profile and the engine's incorporation in an eligible aircraft; (3) services performed on or ancillary to exported goods (e.g., testing, overhaul of an engine destined for export) are exempt under Article 262-I-2° CGI; and (4) offshore B2B leasing services fall outside French VAT where the place of supply is the overseas customer's establishment under Article 259 CGI, with reverse charge in the customer's jurisdiction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (DAU/DES-D2023) lodged electronically via DELTA-G with DGDDI, evidencing removal of the engine from EU territory
Bill of lading or Air Waybill (LTA/AWB) evidencing physical departure and destination outside the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate (attestation de domiciliation bancaire or certificat de change) proving receipt of export proceeds within the 180-day exchange-control period
Commercial export invoice issued by the French SARL stating the VAT exemption or zero-rate basis
Aircraft-engine dry lease agreement defining lease term, rent, delivery terms, maintenance obligations and engine location/return
Packing list, transport insurance certificates and CMR/marine or air transport orders
EUR.1 or equivalent movement certificate where a preferential tariff rate is claimed
Statement of the engine's incorporation into an eligible aircraft and certificate of the airline's predominantly international operations (for Article 262-II-1° CGI)
Temporary import/export declarations where the engine is brought into the EU for operational storage before re-export
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP (fiscal) and DGDDI (customs) audits verify the completeness, coherence and timing of the export evidence. If zero rating or exemption is denied because of missing, forged or late export proof, re-import into France, or artificial trafficking, output VAT is re-assessed at 20% plus late interest (0.20% per month) and penalties: 40% for material inaccuracies, 80% for bad faith (mauvaise foi, Article 1729 CGI) and 100% for tax fraud or abuse of law (Article 1729-b CGI). Criminal sanctions for fiscal fraud under Article 1741 CGI reach EUR 500,000 and 5 years' imprisonment, increased to EUR 3,000,000 and 7 years where committed by an organised gang. For MTIC/carrousel schemes, a claimant who knew or should have known of the fraud loses the right to exemption and may be held jointly liable; customs sanctions include forfeiture and fines of one to two times the evaded duties under the Code des douanes. Non-repatriation of export receivables within 180 days violates the exchange-control domiciliation rules under Articles R. 152-1 et seq. of the Code monétaire et financier, exposing the SARL to administrative fines and reporting to the Banque de France.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (as the French National Central Bank within the Eurosystem), operating under the prudential and regulatory authority of the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) and in coordination with the European Central Bank and European Banking Authority
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full currency convertibility as a Eurozone member. Current-account and capital-account transactions are unrestricted under Articles 63-65 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code Monétaire et Financier). There are no prior administrative authorisations for profit remittance, dividend distributions, or cross-border capital movements, subject to standard banking compliance, tax clearance for large payments under Article L.561-15-1 of the code, and balance-of-payments statistical reporting thresholds administered by Banque de France.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement applies in France or in the Eurozone. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency in French-registered banks indefinitely, and the full amount may be converted freely. For aircraft engine dry-lease companies, lease rental inflows originating from non-resident lessees are treated as ordinary export of services for balance-of-payments purposes; Banque de France requires direct statistical declaration for any transaction exceeding €50,000 or its equivalent when the counterparty is outside the Eurozone.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account denominated in EUR, USD, and major aviation currencies

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow / Asset Finance Collection Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating is LOW for primary treasury operations and MODERATE only as a supplementary collection channel. A French-registered EMI (Établissement de Paiement under the PSD2 / French Monetary and Financial Code) can legally open payment accounts and execute cross-border collections, but cannot grant credit, hold client funds as a bank, or provide sophisticated trade-finance instruments such as commercial LCs. A non-EEA offshore digital EMI (e.g., Volt, or other third-country wallets) is legally unacceptable for the principal corporate treasury function of an aircraft engine lessor, as it will typically not satisfy aerodynamic engine title security, escrow segregation, or Banque de France statistical reporting requirements. It may be used exclusively for small incidental collections pending migration to bank rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French banks do not categorically mandate a physical appearance of all directors where the SARL is French-resident and the signatories are EEA-resident. However, for a non-resident SARL shareholder or for directors whose identify is not verifiable via national registers, the KYC interview is de facto mandatory. The credit institution's internal governance rules under ACPR Recommendation 2014-05 and the French transposition of the 4th/5th AMLD require at least one in-person or notarially certified remote interview for the legal representative and the beneficial owner. A physical meeting in France (or with a French notary/embassy officer for remote certification) is strongly advised before account activation for stage-4 escrow and high-value engine disbursements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity due to licensed-entity or naked-trust structure above the SARL
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete chain of UBO declarations filed with the Registre National des Beneficiaires Effectifs (RBE), updated organizational chart, signed declarations of non-tax-haven status, and audited financial statements of every shareholder with over 25% ownership

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds discomfort regarding initial capital injection or shareholder loan used to purchase two or more aircraft engines with high unit value
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed engine purchase agreements (PHY-A blue book or similar), bank transaction history from the originator bank, title transfer certificates, aircraft registry transcript (F-register or FAA or other registry), notarised shareholder loan deeds, and independent valuation report certifying engine market value correspondence

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions / embargo screening hit on the lessee, ultimate airline, or maintenance vendor (e.g., IRGC, OFAC 50% list, or EU restrictive measures)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Output of daily sanctions-screening log (World-Check or LexisNexis), verification against EU OJ consolidated list and OFAC SDN list, end-user certificate executed by the lessee's board, and a negative-surveillance letter from a reputable checking bureau

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected artificial splitting of lease payments to avoid transaction-level AML reporting or invoke Pandora / shell-indicator red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Engine lease and sublease schedules with unique engine serial number (ESN), full payment waterfall model, assignment of receivables, and an independent auditor's confirmations of economic substance in France (personnel, payroll tax filings, management office, bank-in-France statement)

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction activity near Armenia, Kazakhstan, UAE free zone or other aviation leasing hot spots with perceived custody gap
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Controlled-relationship matrix, physical engine inspection certificates by a neutral third-party (e.g., Aeronautical Engineering Services), battery of lease-return conditions, insurance certificates naming the SARL as insured, and a detailed compliance letter from the lessee's bank confirming vendor payment channel

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection into the French SARL must be effected by wire transfer (SWIFT). For direct investment from an EEA parent, use the standard correspondent-bank routing through TARGET2. For third-country shareholder investment, an MT103 through a long-established clearing bank is required. The purpose code must align with the French balance-of-payments nomenclature (Banque de France 'enquête IMU-OF / catégorie A39'): classification as 'Investissements directs – Capitaux propres' (equity injection / increasing financial participation). If the injection is a shareholder loan, use code 'Crédits commerciaux et opérations assimilées – Prêts de sociétés non-résidentes' or the standard 'Autres investissements – Prêts'. Supporting verification documents are (i) executive board minutes authorising the capital increase, (ii) notarised deed and publication in a French legal gazette, (iii) anti-money-laundering declaration if injected amount exceeds €10,000, (iv) Bank of France receipt of follow-up statistical declaration of capital relationship (liaison financière) if the net liability to non-residents exceeds €250,000, and (v) bank-to-bank verification of the originating account holder.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade disbursements under aircraft engine dry leasing: (i) SWIFT MT103 payments for lease return costs, maintenance transfers (labor and non-labor components), insurance premiums, and individual engine disposition payments; (ii) documentary Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) issued under UCP600 for the purchase or re-purchase of engines / spare parts, with documents required as aircraft registry release, certificate-of-airworthiness, and title/encumbrance certification; (iii) SEPA Credit Transfers for cross-border EUR transactions to EEA vendors used for French aviation suppliers; (iv) high-value multi-currency netting to a global liquidity sweeper via EUR/USD contractor; and (v) automated clearing-house (ACH/SEPA B2B) to regular captive vendors. All payments above €50,000 to non-EEA counterparties require contingent report to Banque de France for external-payment statistics; over €1,000,000 or high-risk jurisdiction payments also require documentary evidence of underlying trade contract, a signed invoice, and the engine ESN in the exception notice to the payment gateway.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Cash-forward outright exchange forwards on EUR/USD and EUR/GBP to lock-in lease rental conversion rates for a defined engine lease period

Euro-future and non-deliverable-forwards (NDF) on USD, as needed for emerging-market lessees denominating rents in USD but settling in EUR line to the SARL's account, expressly permitted for hedge-only operations
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) converting floating USD funding into fixed EUR liability when the engine acquisition is financed through Eurobond or bank debt
European-style premium-adjustable FX options (EUR call / USD put) for contingent hedging of lease residual value
FX swaps (tom/next and outright settled) to manage liquidity between EUR and foreign-currency transit accounts without speculation
Currency swaps with Banque de France-approved credit institutions for long-dated structural exposures (third-country leases extending beyond two years)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and management report deposit (Dépôt des comptes annuels) with legal auditor report if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) via Infogreffe
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end; for calendar-year SARL, shareholders must approve annual accounts by 30 June and file with the registry by 31 July (1 month after approval)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of €1,500 per legal representative for non-filing; court order under Article L247-2; possible injunction with periodic penalty; ultimate radiative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS after 6 months of non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Déclaration de résultats et de détermination de l'impôt sur les sociétés) via Form 2065-SD and supporting schedules 2058-A-SD/2059-G-SD
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) – Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For fiscal year ending 31 December, no later than the 3rd business day after 1 May of the following year; for off-calendar year-ends, within 3 months of the closing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties: 5% monthly surcharge on the corporate tax due (max 40%) plus late-payment interest at 0.2% per month; overstated tax base may trigger 80% penalty plus interest; criminal fine up to €10,000 per director for willful non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owner information (Bénéficiaires effectifs) submitted as part of the annual accounts filing package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI – Registre National des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as annual accounts deposit deadline, i.e., within 7 months after financial year-end or by 31 July for calendar-year SARL; immediate update required within 30 days of any change in shareholding or control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal sanctions under Article L561-7 of the Monetary and Financial Code: up to 6 months imprisonment and €30,000 fine for the legal representative for false or incomplete declarations; the registry may also block registration of further filings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local business tax (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises – CFE) annual franchise payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP – Local Tax Office (Service des Impôts des Particuliers for property-based taxes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payment due by 15 December of the tax year; a CFE declaration (Form 1447-C) is only renewed if activity, premises, or shareholders change, otherwise assessed automatically on prior-year rental values
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment surcharge plus 0.2% monthly interest; forced collection through tax enforcement (avis à tiers détenteur); additional penalties for under-declaration of basis

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) must appoint a statutory auditor (Commissaire aux Comptes) if, at the financial year-end, it exceeds at least two of the three thresholds: total assets €4,000,000, turnover (HT) €8,000,000, or 50 average employees; voluntary appointment is also permitted by shareholder resolution or in companies controlling or controlled by another legal entity
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles – Règlement Général de l'Autorité des Normes Comptables (ANC) 2016-06 (PCG); non-consolidated accounts of a SARL are prepared under French GAAP, not IFRS, unless consolidated statements are required

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a separate annual UBO refresher filing; instead, accuracies of the beneficial owner register (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) must be certified each year when the annual accounts are filed with the Greffe. Any transfer of shares or change in direct or indirect control triggers a mandatory update within 30 days. The official registry is the Registre National des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), and no additional corporate-level UBO declaration is needed for a standard SARL unless a change occurs
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders / share transfer register (Registre des mouvements de titres) – must record all share issuance and transfers
Register of corporate decisions and minutes of shareholders' meetings (Registre des procès-verbaux d'assemblées et de décisions) including attendance sheets (feuilles de présence)
Register of statutory auditor's attendance (if a Commissaire aux Comptes is appointed) – minutes of meetings must evidence auditor presence
Beneficial owner information file (RBE) maintained at registered office summarizing the declaration transmitted to the registry

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$ 350 – 1,100 per year for a professional registered-office service in France (Paris and major cities at the higher end)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$ 5,500 – 16,000 per year for an independent statutory audit when mandated; zero if the SARL remains below the compulsory audit thresholds and does not voluntarily appoint a Commissaire aux Comptes

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard corporate income tax rate applicable from 1 January 2022)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on taxable profits up to EUR 42,000 per fiscal year for SMEs meeting turnover and ownership tests; Research Tax Credit (Crédit d'Impôt Recherche, CIR) of 30% on eligible R&D expenditures up to EUR 100 million; Innovation Tax Credit (Crédit d'Impôt Innovation, CII) at 30% of eligible innovation expenses; Patent Box regime enabling an effective tax rate of 5% on qualifying industrial property income; accelerated depreciation for long-life aircraft engines and certain aviation assets; option for group tax consolidation (intégration fiscale) for SARL members of a French tax group.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CERFA 2065-SD (annual corporate income tax return) accompanied by the 'liasse fiscale' comprising forms 2050 to 2059-A. Filed electronically via the TDFC (TéléDéclaration Française des Commissions) facility on the official French tax portal impots.gouv.fr or through the EFI (Échange de Formulaires Informatisé) portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. In addition to the annual return, four quarterly advance payments of corporate income tax are required on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December using form 2571.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the annual return must be filed by 3 May of the following year. For a fiscal year not ending on 31 December, the return must be filed within three months of the fiscal year-end. The definitive annual tax balance and any balance due are payable upon filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SIREN company registration number, APE/NAF code assigned from the principal activity, and tax office reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the French SIREN of the SARL; if a foreign company has a French permanent establishment, provide the foreign corporate identifier and the French PE address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the applicable tax regime: corporate income tax (IS) or income tax (IR). A SARL engaged in aircraft engine leasing is subject to IS by default.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tick the IS box. Non-resident SARLs owning French-sourced assets are also subject to IS on French-source income unless a treaty allocation applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit and loss account: operating income, rents from dry leasing of aircraft engines, depreciation charges, other operating expenses and financial income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only French-source lease income and directly allocable expenses; transfer pricing adjustments must be booked consistently with the arm's length principle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting profit to taxable income: adds non-deductible expenses, deducts exempt income, tax credits, depreciation adjustments and prior-year loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident must include any taxable permanent establishment income and cannot offset foreign losses against French-source profits absent a treaty provision.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of tax credits such as CIR, CII, or foreign tax credits computed under domestic law or double tax treaties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident SARL may claim treaty foreign tax credits only for French-source income; R&D credits are available only for research conducted in France.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or failure to file (défaut de dépôt) incurs a sole penalty (majoration) of 10% of the tax due if the return is filed within 30 days after the deadline, rising to 40% if filed later or after formal notice. Late payment interest (intérêt de retard) is 0.2% of the unpaid tax for each month of delay. An additional 5% late payment surcharge applies after the expiry of a 30-day formal payment demand. Penalties can be mitigated by prompt correction or a first-time taxpayer defence.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% for dividends distributed to non-resident legal entities under Article 119 bis 2 of the French General Tax Code (CGI). For non-resident individual shareholders, the withholding tax rate is 12.8%, with an additional 17.2% social levies in certain cross-border cases.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced rate under a double tax agreement (DTA), the non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign competent authority and submit it to the French paying company or to the French tax office before the payment date. The administrative procedure requires filing Forms 2561 (normal withholding relief) or 2561 Bis (simplified relief for treaty-abiding countries) via the FICO claim platform on impots.gouv.fr. For dividends, the paying company applies the treaty rate if the claim is accepted; refund of excess withholding is available through Form 2577. The beneficial owner must satisfy treaty limitation-on-benefits clauses and the Anti-Abuse Principal Purpose Test under the MLI.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French domestic law subjects royalties paid by a French company to non-residents to a 25% withholding tax (Article 182 B CGI). Interest paid on loans between non-banking entities may also face a 25% withholding tax (Article 125 A CGI), though interest paid on commercial bank credit is often exempt. Treaty rates commonly reduce interest to 0% or 10% and royalties to 0% or 5%, depending on the DTA paired with the residence country. For aircraft engine dry leasing, the income may be characterized as 'leasing' rather than royalty if the EUR arrangement transfers no IP; French and OECD commentary should be followed to avoid recharacterization.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50 million annual net turnover (excluding VAT) or total balance-sheet assets of EUR 50 million triggers the Local File obligation for the French SARL. Master File is mandatory when the French entity belongs to a group with consolidated annual group turnover exceeding EUR 750 million. Country-by-Country Report filing threshold is EUR 750 million group revenue (or equivalent in EUR).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations as a lex specialis; instead, economic substance is governed by general anti-abuse rules and treaty principles. The SARL must demonstrate de facto management and control in France (Article 209 CGI) to maintain French tax residency. For treaty benefits, the Principal Purpose Test denies relief when the arrangement lacks genuine business purpose, and the doctrine of 'abus de droit' (LPF Article L64) permits the tax administration to disregard artificial transactions lacking legitimate substance. Specifically for aircraft engine dry leasing, sufficient physical presence, custodian or maintenance contracts, local staff, and decision-making in France are required to avoid a finding of a shell company or sucursale abroad. The French patent box regime also requires IFRS-defined IP ownership and active R&D in France for the 5% effective rate.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of dry lease rental income, falsification of balance sheet accounts, destruction of accounting records, or use of specialised software to mask turnover derived from aircraft engine leasing operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to EUR 1.5 million; aggravated fraud (committed by an organised gang) increases the fine to EUR 3 million and imprisonment from 7 to 10 years. The tax authority adds an evasion penalty of 80% of the evaded tax (Article 1729-1 CGI), plus late payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be criminally imprisoned, subject to travel bans (interdiction de quitter le territoire), and personally liable for civil restitution of unpaid taxes and penalties; a management ban and confiscation of assets are also possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of Law / Artificial Arrangement (Abus de Droit)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing an opaque structure, such as an intermediary holding company or SPV, that holds the dry-leased aircraft engine but is wholly devoid of economic substance, staff, budgeting, and asset risk; payments are routed purely for tax avoidance, or treaty-shopping relief is sought without real commercial purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: If the tax authority successfully invokes LPF Article L64, the transaction is recharacterized, resulting in a 80% penalty applied to the resulting tax adjustment, plus 0.2% monthly late-payment interest; criminal prosecution for fraud may also follow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held civilly liable for the tax deficiency under the shadow-management doctrine, and criminal penalties include imprisonment up to 3 years and fines of up to EUR 750,000; prohibition from conducting a commercial activity for 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Master File, Local File, or Country-by-Country Report in France when thresholds are met, or submitting intercompany lease rental rates that materially deviate from arm's-length pricing for the turbo-fan engine type and operational risk profile.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine of EUR 10,000 for non-filing of CbCR (Article 1729 E CGI); for TP documentation failure, a fine of up to 5% of the amount of the reassessed profit after tax adjustment, or up to 5% of the omitted taxable base, plus 0.2% monthly interest. Profits may be reallocated to France from the related party.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil procedures for the adjustment; in cases where documents are falsified or used to hide unrepatriated profits, exposure exists for fraud and personal liability for fines and interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receipt of aircraft engine lease payments through escrow accounts or SWIFT wires without conducting adequate beneficial-ownership verification, failure to file Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) to TRACFIN, or deliberately concealing cross-border beneficial ownership of the SARL.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine under the Monetary and Financial Code (CMF) of up to EUR 3 million for entities and EUR 750,000 for individuals; judicial criminal fine for money laundering up to EUR 5 million and imprisonment of 5 years. The ACPR may additionally suspend or withdraw the SARL's authorisation to conduct aviation asset leasing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally face criminal imprisonment up to 5 years, fines, prohibition from employment, and confiscation of assets; civil liability covers damages and restitution of illegal flows. Travel bans may be ordered to prevent cross-border concealment.
